version.changelog: Sync skill instructions, references, and helper from GitHub 4164b4f6c8272e152ee99cbafd3d88b4549533e3

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed research workflow that sends user-chosen search and social-media queries to Crawlora, with bounded endpoints and no evidence of hidden persistence or unrelated data access.

dimensions.detail: It requires network access to api.crawlora.net and a CRAWLORA_API_KEY, which is expected for the advertised API-backed research workflow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill includes an executable shell helper and does not declare a separate allowed-tools or permissions manifest, but the helper itself restricts routes, methods, base URL, and argument handling.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions emphasize bounded samples, source limits, no demand-score invention, retry limits, and stopping on authentication errors.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background worker, system service, privilege escalation, credential store access, or local indexing behavior was found; the temporary curl config is removed on exit.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is topic-demand validation using autocomplete, Trends, SERP, Reddit, TikTok, and YouTube samples; the bundled helper and endpoint reference match that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending the topics, search queries, and selected public post/video IDs you ask it to research to Crawlora, and remember successful API calls may be billable against your Crawlora account. Avoid using it with confidential product ideas unless that external API use is acceptable.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill invokes a bundled shell helper; the absence of explicit permission metadata is a packaging gap, but the artifact shows a narrow helper with fixed API base, route allowlisting, and method checks.
[E1] expected: External transmission to Crawlora is disclosed and necessary for the skill's search and social-data collection purpose; the helper sends the API key as a header and query/body values only to allowed Crawlora endpoints.
[PE2] unexpected: The cited chmod 600 sets restrictive permissions on a temporary curl config file and does not invoke sudo, root, or privilege escalation.
